forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,65 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M0SVAZ3WJH2BQFJSA6E4X8NW
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '9480'
+title: Make the SeatbeltSandbox docs state that the sandbox is the whole gate
+---
+## What
+
+`Sources/FoundationModelsMultitool/Capabilities/Shell/SeatbeltSandbox.swift` was
+written on the assumption that a policy layer stands in front of it. Two doc
+sites defer to a type that no longer exists:
+
+- **Lines 6-10**, the file header: *"WHETHER a command runs at all stays the
+  decision of `ShellPolicy`. This layer bounds only what a command that already
+  went through the policy can do."*
+- **Lines 245-248**, the network paragraph: *"To bound which commands can run at
+  all — network tools included — stays with `ShellPolicy`."*
+
+Both are now false. There is no policy. The sandbox is the whole gate.
+
+Rewrite both so they describe the real posture, and state the boundary honestly
+rather than pointing at a layer that is gone. The profile itself does not change
+— only the text that explains it. What the profile truly gives, measured from
+`sandboxProfile` at lines 260-273:
+
+- `(deny default)` with the least allowances that let `/bin/sh` start.
+- **Writing and deleting are bounded** to the granted subpaths. This is the one
+  real guard, and it is enforced by the kernel, thus how the command is spelled
+  does not matter.
+- **Every read is free**, everywhere. `(allow file-read*)` is unconditional and
+  there is no `deny file-read*` of any kind.
+- **The network is fully open**: `(allow network*)` and `(allow system-socket)`.
+
+State the consequence plainly, because a reader must not think the sandbox
+covers more than it does: a command can read any file the user can read and send
+it anywhere. Destruction is bounded; reading and exfiltration are not. Name the
+place that would change it — the profile — and not a policy layer.
+
+Do not add a read policy or a network policy in this task. The design decision
+is that the sandbox bounds writing and deleting. This task makes the docs match
+that decision.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `SeatbeltSandbox.swift` names `ShellPolicy` nowhere.
+- [ ] The header states that the sandbox is the only gate.
+- [ ] The docs state that reads are free and the network is open, and name the
+      exfiltration consequence.
+- [ ] The docs name the profile as the place to change either one.
+- [ ] `sandboxProfile` emits byte-identical text to before this task.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/SeatbeltSandboxTests.swift` — a test
+      asserts the emitted profile text is unchanged, thus a doc rewrite cannot
+      change behavior by accident.
+- [ ] `swift test --filter SeatbeltSandbox` passes.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes with no new failure and no new warning.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the profile-text guard first, watch it pass before and
+  after, then rewrite the docs. #phase-2 #eventplan
\ No newline at end of file
